name: explainer
title: Explainer
summary: A 60-to-120-second film that makes one idea, product or process clear: the problem, the idea, how it works, the proof and the next step.
use_when: Someone needs to understand how a thing works, fast, from a website, a landing page, YouTube or LinkedIn.

pace.note: The films' placement; an explainer is spoken almost wall to wall, so the ceiling matters more than the lead.

beats.name: problem
beats.job: The problem in the viewer's own words, and what it costs them.

beats.name: idea
beats.job: The idea that solves it, in one sentence.

beats.name: how it works
beats.job: At most three steps, each one shown working.

beats.name: proof
beats.job: One sourced number or a real result.

beats.name: next step
beats.job: What to do now, and where.

rules: One idea per shot; if a shot needs two labels and a paragraph, it's two shots.
Show each step working instead of listing it.
Every number is sourced or on the brand's approved-claims list.

captions.position: drawn by the player from the sidecar files
captions.note: Social cut-downs of an explainer burn their captions in (their own format says so).

budget.note: 0-2 generated shots at about $15-30 each, including one reject.

notes: LinkedIn plays 16:9 in the feed; a square or 4:5 LinkedIn cut is a derived film in the linkedin format.
